target.title: feat: support GCP broker metadata auth
target.body:
## Summary

- Adds explicit `CRABBOX_GCP_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE=metadata` support for brokered GCP coordinators running with an attached Google Cloud service identity.
- Preserves service-account-key auth as the default and fails closed for partial key pairs, invalid source names, or keyless config without explicit metadata opt-in.
- Applies source-specific token refresh skew: five minutes for metadata credentials and one minute for service-account keys, so short-lived key tokens remain cacheable.
- Rejects metadata redirects and responses without Google's `Metadata-Flavor: Google` marker before trusting a token.
- Retries connection/startup failures plus transient `429`, `499`, and all `5xx` responses with exponential backoff, a five-second attempt timeout covering headers and body, and a one-minute overall deadline.
- Preserves the HTTP status for non-JSON errors and reports the effective credential source in readiness diagnostics.
- Updates environment typing, provider docs, and regression coverage without retaining a contributor-branch changelog edit.

Refs https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/1016.

## Config and secret implications

Google-hosted coordinators can set `CRABBOX_GCP_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE=metadata` plus `GCP_PROJECT_ID` or `CRABBOX_GCP_PROJECT`. Portable coordinators continue to use both `GCP_CLIENT_EMAIL` and `GCP_PRIVATE_KEY`. Metadata mode sends no Crabbox credential to the metadata endpoint; it makes the documented fixed-host request with `Metadata-Flavor: Google` and uses the returned short-lived access token only for Google Compute API calls.

## Verification

Exact head: `9f22a0dcf33d9528cd7e392c09d31aef6a945655`

- GCP/Fleet focused Worker tests: 471/471 passed.
- Full Worker tests: 947 passed, 3 skipped.
- Worker format, lint, TypeScript checks, Node checks, Wrangler build, and Node build passed.
- AutoReview passed on the local repair and the complete branch diff with no accepted or actionable findings.
- Exact-head hosted CI: [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/actions/runs/29075714075) 7/7 passed; [Connector E2E run](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/actions/runs/29075714169) 5/5 passed.
- Exact-head Blacksmith proof: [run](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/actions/runs/29075975510), provider `blacksmith-testbox`, lease `tbx_01kx5dx8ac2fvggph0f46arh2j`. Ephemeral Node 22.14 ran `npm ci` with zero vulnerabilities, all 471 focused tests, TypeScript checking, and Wrangler build in 75.172 seconds. Exact SHA and a clean tree were asserted before and after; the temporary proof ref was deleted and the lease inventory returned to zero.
- Endpoint, response-marker, token-cache, source-default, access-scope, and retry contracts were checked against current official Compute Engine documentation.

## Live proof and remaining gate

An earlier provider-code candidate ran on a real GCP `e2-standard-2` lease. With only `CRABBOX_GCP_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE=metadata` and the metadata-derived project ID, the bundled `GCPClient` acquired the attached service-account token and completed a real aggregated Compute instance-list request:

```text
metadata_token_acquisition=ok compute_api_request=ok crabbox_machine_count=0
```

At prior exact head `0df05f2b36636866fcc52ec6386f41eb2a3630d4`, a fresh real `e2-standard-2` lease verified the SHA-256 of `worker/src/gcp.ts` before execution. The exact code acquired a real metadata token and reached the Compute API, then failed closed at `compute.firewalls.get` because the attached project-default service account lacked Compute IAM. The diagnostics also proved broker-created VMs have no attached service account unless one is requested explicitly.

Every GCP diagnostic/canary lease was deleted, and provider inventory returned to zero after each attempt. No static GCP key was copied into a lease, and no token was printed or persisted.

The remaining live gate is a full create/use/delete lifecycle at exact head with an attached service account that has the documented Compute IAM permissions and `cloud-platform` access, or an explicit maintainer waiver based on the earlier full Compute proof plus exact-head metadata-token, hosted, and Blacksmith proof. Do not merge until one of those conditions is met.
